title: Predictive Capacity & Model Degradation Mitigation Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook defines detection, triage, mitigation, and customer communication workflows for incidents where model quality or serving capacity degrades in ways that could impact enterprise customers. It is intended for Customer Success (CS), SRE, and Oncall Engineers supporting Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. The goal is to detect early, reduce customer-facing impact quickly, and provide consistent post-incident follow-up and remediation.

Scope:
- Applies to any production event that causes: sustained model output quality regressions affecting customer prompts, or sustained throughput/latency degradation that violates customer SLOs for 5+ minutes.
- Covers Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Excludes scheduled maintenance if communicated per the Maintenance Notification SOP.

Ownership and Contacts:
- Primary owner: Customer Success (Oncall CS lead)
- Secondary owners: SRE (oncall), Serving Runtime (oncall)
- Pager rotation: see internal rota (link in related_pages).
- Escalation contacts:
  - CS Lead (tier1): cs-lead@redwood.example (placeholder)
  - SRE Pager (tier2): +1-800-XXX-XXXX (internal)
  - Runtime Eng (tier3): runtime-oncall@redwood.example

Early Warning Signals (metrics & thresholds):
- Quality signals (synthetic prompt set failures): >10% drop in fidelity score vs baseline across 5-minute window.
- Latency signals: P95 latency > 500ms for 5m or P99 > 2s.
- Error rate: 5xx rate > 2% sustained for 5m.
- Throughput anomalies: sustained CPU/GPU utilization > 85% on Dedicated worker pool for 10m, or request queuing spikes >50 concurrent queued requests.
- Cost anomaly: per-token cost increase >30% vs 24h rolling median.
- Customer reports: 2+ independent customer tickets referencing degraded outputs or throttled requests within 15 minutes.

Detection sources:
- Monitoring dashboards: Customer-Impact Overview, Model-Quality Synthetics, Dedicated-Pool Health (links in dashboards-and-alerts).
- Alerts: quality-regression-high, dedicated-pool-saturation, hosted-error-spike.
- Customer reports: Level-1 CS triage form and initial slack channel (#cs-incidents).

Triage Workflow (first 15 minutes):
1. Acknowledge and classify: CS oncall acknowledges the alert and assigns severity (S1: customer-facing outage, S2: degraded experience, S3: intermittent).
2. Collect breadcrumbs: customer IDs affected, deployment type (hosted/dedicated/private), model version, recent deploys/rollouts, and relevant dashboard links.
3. Quick checks (do in parallel):
   - Check synthetic quality dashboard and compare to previous 24h baseline.
   - Confirm if rollout/canary was active in the last 30 minutes.
   - Verify Dedicated pool utilization and autoscaler events.
   - For Private deployments, check customer VPN/K8s node health via support instrumentation.
4. If S1, escalate to SRE and Runtime Eng immediately; open incident channel (#inc-<ticket-id>) and mark customer POCs.

Mitigation Playbooks (ordered by low-customer-impact preference):
A) Rapid routing / traffic shaping (Hosted & Dedicated):
  - Route traffic to a known-stable model variant (example: model-v2 -> model-v1-fallback) using routing policy override in the Control Plane.
  - CLI example: redwoodctl routing override --customer <customer_id> --from model-v2 --to model-v1-fallback --ttl 30m
  - Validate outputs with 5 synthetic prompts before notifying customer.

B) Scale & capacity temporary measures (Dedicated):
  - Increase autoscaler max_burst by +25% for the affected pool.
  - If autoscale is saturated, contact capacity-ops to provision pre-warmed nodes (follow Reserved Burst SOP).
  - Commands (internal): kubectl scale --replicas=<n> deploy/dedicated-pool-<id> --namespace=prod-serving

C) Kill faulty rollout / rollback (Hosted & Dedicated):
  - If a new model or runtime release correlates with regression, trigger immediate rollback to previous model image and revert config flags.
  - Follow Release Reversion checklist: confirm commit, tag previous model, and validate smoke tests.

D) Customer-level throttles & temporary quotas:
  - Apply per-customer rate limits to reduce queueing for other tenants while preserving SLAs for highest-tier customers.
  - redwoodctl tenants update --id <customer_id> --quota-rps 2

E) Private deployment-specific mitigations:
  - If customer onprem processes are saturated, provide a temporary routing plan: enable customer to use Hosted fallback (if contractual).
  - Provide a curated troubleshooting bundle (logs, KV-cache state export, recommended config changes) and schedule a joint call with onprem eng.

Customer Communication templates (use CS portal to send; customize where needed):
- Initial acknowledgment (within 30m):
  "We are aware of elevated latency/quality issues affecting your requests to <model>. Our engineering and SRE teams are investigating. We will provide an update within 60 minutes or sooner if there is a material change."
- Status update (every 60m for ongoing incident):
  "We have applied a temporary routing change to stabilize outputs and are validating results on your prompt set. Next update in 60 minutes. If you want to test before then, we can run your test set on the fallback model immediately."
- Post-incident summary (within 48h):
  "Summary: root cause, impact window, customers affected, mitigation applied, permanent fix timeline, and any customer actions required (none/upgrade tokens/verify prompts)."

Validation & Rollout of Quick Fixes:
- Run a 10-sample smoke test of customer-critical prompts against the target model and capture scores (fidelity/label match).
- Approval: CS lead + SRE lead must sign off before reverting routing. Use the Incident Tracker to attach test results.

Post-Incident Steps (RCA and remediation):
1. Assign RCA lead within 24 hours (preferably SRE or Runtime Eng).
2. Gather artifact bundle: alert timelines, deploy logs, synthetic test results, export of KV cache stats, sample customer prompts with outputs.
3. Run RCA timeline and root cause analysis; target RCA publish within 5 business days.
4. Action items: assign owners, remediation deadlines, and risk mitigations. Track via the Reliability Board.

Runbook Checklist (table):
| Item | Threshold | Immediate Action | Owner |
|-----|-----------:|------------------|------|
| Quality drop (synthetic) | >10% vs baseline | Route to fallback model; notify customer | CS/SRE |
| P95 latency | >500ms (5m) | Scale pool; apply throttles | SRE |
| 5xx errors | >2% (5m) | Rollback recent release; engage runtime eng | Runtime Eng |
| Pool util (GPU) | >85% (10m) | Burst provision or reduce capacity using throttles | Capacity Ops |

(Represented above as plain text table for Confluence).

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Customer Success: customer comms, impact assessment, and verification of customer-specific prompts.
- SRE: triage infrastructure, autoscaling, and global routing changes.
- Serving Runtime: investigate kernel/runtime regressions and model execution issues.
- Capacity Ops: provisioning and reserved bursts with cloud provider.

Postmortem and Customer Follow-up Guidance:
- Publish postmortem summary to affected customers and internal stakeholders within 5 business days. Include the following sections: impact summary, cause, mitigation applied, permanent fix, timeline, and customer-facing mitigations (if any).
- Offer a remediation call within 7 days for enterprise customers with SLA credits or contractual remedies if impacted.

Preventative Measures & Continuous Improvements:
- Add synthetic prompt coverage for on-call customers to the Model-Quality suite (Product/CS coordinated).
- Quarterly load-tests on Dedicated pools with production-like traffic from known enterprise tenants.
- Maintain a small catalog of verified fallback model variants for each major model family.

Appendix: Useful commands & snippets:
- Quick traffic override: redwoodctl routing override --customer <customer_id> --from <model> --to <fallback_model> --ttl 30m
- Example synthetic check (pseudo):
  curl -s -X POST https://monitoring.internal/api/synthetics/run -d '{"customer_id":"<id>","prompts":["..."],"model":"<model>"}'

- Minimal YAML for autoscaler tweak (example):
  apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
  kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
  metadata:
    name: dedicated-pool-<id>-hpa
  spec:
    maxReplicas: 60
    minReplicas: 4
    metrics: [...]

Document history and links:
- Owners should update this playbook after every S1 incident that required routing changes or capacity bursts.
- Cross-link to: dashboards, incident tracker, and Release Reversion checklist in architecture-and-standards.

End of playbook.
